title: SOURCE_TARGETS retired: infoschema masking-policy loader uses sys executor factory, not user session

analysis: LoadMaskingPolicies obtains a session resource from infoSchema.factory, then uses ExecRestrictedSQL with ExecOptionUseCurSession on that resource
the factory stored in infoSchema is passed by infoschema.NewBuilder from issyncer.Loader.sysExecutorFactory
domain.Init wires loader.sysExecutorFactory to do.sysExecutorFactory(do), and session/tidb.go passes getSessionFactoryWithDom(store) as sysFactory
getSessionFactoryInternal creates a separate internal session, sets InRestrictedSQL=true, and does not copy the user session's TxnReadTS or SnapshotInfoschema
ExecOptionUseCurSession here means the masking-policy query stays on the internal/sys session borrowed from the factory; it does not mean the user statement's session is reused
source_anchors: pkg/infoschema/infoschema.go:715 loads policies via LoadMaskingPolicies(is.factory, is.ts)
pkg/infoschema/infoschema.go:753-784 obtains resource := factory(), casts to sessionctx.Context, and calls ExecRestrictedSQL with ExecOptionUseCurSession
pkg/infoschema/issyncer/loader.go:273 and :360 pass l.sysExecutorFactory into infoschema.NewBuilder
pkg/session/tidb.go:101-122 passes getSessionFactoryWithDom(store) as sysFactory to domain.Init
pkg/session/session.go:1312-1354 getSessionFactoryInternal creates an internal session and marks InRestrictedSQL=true
payload.why_not_execute: A RED would require injecting pending TxnReadTS into the sys executor factory session or treating lazy InfoSchema loading as if it reused the user's session. That would test the harness assumption rather than a product-feasible user schedule.
payload.next_step: keep as negative cache for state-ingress generator; continue with lower-priority dynamic candidates whose session ownership is not already explained by sys/internal factories
